_about: MCP_MEMORY_PLAN stage 5, the live test with fresh examples (11-19 afternoon): labels written before the run. One invented person per round, each planted the same, so the rounds don't feed each other: A for ChatGPT with Recollect left unselected, B for ChatGPT with it selected from '+', C for claude.ai. The one-time preference line is set in each site's settings; the chats never name Recollect. 'expect' is what a good assistant passes on; 'accept' lists other filings that are still right. Fresh topics only (no walking, Spanish, guitar, pottery, running, swimming or study).

chats.purpose: A long work chat; a day's progress on a followed thing at message 3; work details and venting after it

messages.text: I'm debugging consumer lag on a Kafka topic at work. What are the usual causes when lag grows only during peak hours?
We have 12 partitions and 4 consumers in the group. Would adding consumers help, or is it more about processing time per message?
Side note, did my yoga this morning before logging on, 40 minutes. Anyway: how do I measure per-message processing time without changing much code?
accept: remember linked as done on yoga
messages.why: one day's doing of the followed yoga thread; answers its open question

messages.text: The group is payments-settlement-v2 on the client's cluster and lag peaks around 1.2M messages at 7pm. Does max.poll.records matter here?
Honestly my lead keeps changing priorities every sprint and it's exhausting. Can you sketch a quick checklist I can run tomorrow?
messages.why: work venting stays in the chat

messages.text: Thanks. Last one: should I alert on lag in messages or in seconds?

chats.purpose: A long work chat; a real change of routine and a new interest halfway through

messages.text: I need to write a short design doc for a rate limiter in our API gateway. Can you outline the sections?
We're choosing between token bucket and sliding window log. Which fits bursty mobile clients better?
Makes sense. Unrelated, but I've stopped reading before bed, I listen to audiobooks on my commute instead now. Back to the doc: where should the limiter state live, Redis or in memory?
accept: update read dropped plus remember the audiobooks
messages.why: a real change of routine of a known habit

messages.text: We run 6 gateway pods behind an ALB, around 3k requests per second at peak. Does that change your answer?
Oh, and I've gotten into birdwatching lately, went to the lake on Sunday with binoculars. For the doc, what failure mode should I call out if Redis is down?
accept: remember with kind pattern or preference
messages.why: a new interest, never linked to a followed thing

messages.text: Great, can you draft the 'Alternatives considered' section in five bullets?

messages.text: Can you review this Go function? func sum(xs []int) (t int) { for _, x := range xs { t += x }; return } Anything unidiomatic?

Ugh, I had two coffees already today, the cutting down isn't going great. Anyway, how do I test that errors.Is matches my wrapped error?
messages.why: one day's slip on the coffee aim: day news, never a change or an end

messages.text: Also I've pulled out of the charity ride in December, my knee can't take the training. Back to Go: table-driven tests or separate test functions for 5 error cases?
messages.why: the end of a known aim

messages.text: The service is the billing reconciler for our client in Rotterdam and it runs nightly at 2am. Any tips for logging in a batch job like that?
